proof_review.folding: In the quotient z^p=I, z=x(1-u) gives u^p=0. Inverting the binomial basis and setting k=p-j yields exactly [u^(p-m-1)](1-u)^(m-2)G; all indices lie in the audited range.
proof_review.local_logarithm: Writing T=1+z^2 gives B0=-sum_(j=1)^(p-1)T^j/j and T=u(2-u), hence B0(x(1-u))=u A_p(u). The target bounds n_nu<=p-4 make the square-coefficient identity denominator-safe.
proof_review.pearson: The four distinct local linears multiply to 4-10u+10u^2-5u^3+u^4. Coefficient extraction from D H'=N H has pivot 4n for every required 1<=n<p.
proof_review.tail_factor: The target exceeds the lambda=0 input degree by R=r+1, so lambda=0,...,r are exact roots. Termwise falling-factor extraction gives the two harmonic moment formulas and the division-free determinant identity without assuming either G_nu(0) is nonzero.
proof_review.split_scope: For p=1 mod 4 a nonzero pair a+bI may vanish at one root; rootwise zero is norm zero, not pair equality. The p=109 and p=149 witnesses therefore disprove only a universal Wronskian-unit argument, not joint nonvanishing of the original factors.
proof_review.booking: This leading-factor analysis concerns the stronger p^3 terminal route and supplies no ordinary p^2 capacity reduction or exponent.
